steps.body: To say a decimal in words, read the digits after the point as a whole number, then name the **last** (smallest) place. So 0.375 is "three hundred seventy-five **thousandths**" — because the last digit lands in thousandths. One place name covers the whole fractional part.

widget.prompt: 0.28 is read "twenty-eight ___." Which place name fills the blank?

options.label: hundredths
options.feedback: The last digit (8) is in the hundredths place, so the whole thing is twenty-eight hundredths.

options.label: tenths
options.feedback: Tenths would be a one-place decimal. 0.28 runs to the second place, so it's twenty-eight hundredths.

options.label: thousandths
options.feedback: Thousandths is the third place; 0.28 only reaches the second. It's twenty-eight hundredths.

options.label: twenty-eighths
options.feedback: "Twenty-eighths" isn't a decimal place. Read the digits (28) then name the last place: hundredths.

hints: Read the digits after the point as a number: 28.
explanationVariants: The last place (hundredths) names it: twenty-eight hundredths.

predict.prompt: Reading a decimal aloud — which place gives the read its NAME?

options.label: The place of the LAST digit

predict.reveal: The final digit's place christens the whole read — the name comes from where the number ENDS, however many digits it took to get there.

explanationVariants: 0.6 has one place — tenths — so it's six tenths.
The last (only) place is tenths: six tenths.

widget.prompt: How do you say 0.6 in words?

commonBuilds.feedback: Six hundredths is 0.06. With one place, 0.6 is six tenths.
Sixty hundredths equals 0.60, which is the same value — but read at its own last place, 0.6 is six tenths.
Plain six is the whole number. 0.6 is a fraction of one: six tenths.

widget.missFeedback: One digit after the point means the last place is tenths — name the digit, then the place.
widget.successFeedback: One digit after the point, in tenths: six tenths.

steps.body: Going the other way, the place name tells you the **last** place to fill — and you may need placeholder zeros to reach it. "Nine hundredths" ends in hundredths (2nd place), so the 9 goes there and a 0 holds the empty tenths: **0.09**.

explanationVariants: "Nine hundredths" puts 9 in the hundredths place; the empty tenths needs a 0: 0.09.
Hundredths is the second place, so 9 lands there and 0 holds the first: 0.09.

commonErrors.feedback: 0.9 is nine TENTHS. Nine hundredths needs the 9 one place further right, with a 0 in tenths: 0.09.
0.009 is nine thousandths, the third place. Hundredths is the second place: 0.09.
9.0 is the whole number nine. Nine hundredths is a small fraction of one: 0.09.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Hundredths is the SECOND place after the point — a 0 holds the tenths.
widget.successFeedback: Hundredths is the second place, so the 9 goes there and a 0 holds the tenths: 0.09.

steps.body: Match each decimal to its words.

widget.prompt: Match each decimal to how it's read aloud.

pairErrors.feedback: Five tenths is 0.5. 0.09 reads by its last place, hundredths: nine hundredths.

widget.missFeedback: Read the digits as a number, then name the last (smallest) place.

explanationVariants: In a mixed number the word 'and' marks the decimal point: 2.5 is 'two and five tenths'.
'And' separates the whole part from the fractional part — it IS the point, spoken.

widget.prompt: How do you read 2.5 aloud, place-value style?

commonBuilds.feedback: Place-value reading uses 'and' for the point, not the word 'point': two and five tenths.
Twenty-five tenths is 2.5 as a single fraction (25/10) — true in value, but read place-by-place it's two and five tenths.
The fractional part still needs its place name: two and five TENTHS.

widget.missFeedback: Say the whole part, 'and' for the point, then the fraction part with its place name.
widget.successFeedback: The word 'and' marks the decimal point: two [point] five tenths.

hints: Find the last place named: thousandths (third place).
So the digits fill up to the third place after the point.
'Three hundred seventy-five' is 375, ending in thousandths.
explanationVariants: 'Three hundred seventy-five thousandths' is 375/1000 — the 375 fills through the thousandths place: 0.375.
The last place is thousandths, and 375 fills the three places: 0.375.

widget.prompt: Write "three hundred seventy-five thousandths" as a decimal.

commonErrors.feedback: That pushes 375 too far right. Ending in thousandths means the LAST digit is in the third place — 375 fits exactly: 0.375.
That's the whole number. 'Thousandths' makes it a fraction of one: 0.375.
3.75 reads as 'three and seventy-five hundredths.' The given words end in thousandths: 0.375.

widget.fallbackFeedback: The words end in thousandths, so the LAST digit of 375 sits in the third place.
widget.successFeedback: 375 ending in the thousandths place fills all three places: 0.375.

takeaways: Say a decimal by reading its digits as a number, then naming the last (smallest) place.
Words back to a decimal: fill up to the named last place, using placeholder zeros as needed.
In a mixed number, the word 'and' marks the decimal point.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Read the digits after the point as a whole number, then name the last place.** 0.7 → seven tenths (last place is tenths). 0.07 → seven hundredths (last place is hundredths). The last digit's place names the whole fraction.

explanationVariants: 0.7 ends in the tenths place — seven tenths.
One digit after the point is tenths: seven tenths.

widget.prompt: How do you say 0.7 in words?

options.label: seven tenths
options.feedback: One place after the point is tenths: seven tenths.

options.label: seven hundredths
options.feedback: Seven hundredths is 0.07. 0.7 has one place: seven tenths.

options.label: seven
options.feedback: Plain seven is the whole number. 0.7 is seven tenths.
